name: Python Pickle __reduce__
description: Python's pickle module calls __reduce__ or __reduce_ex__ on objects during deserialization. A malicious object can return a tuple of (callable, args) that executes arbitrary code when unpickled.
attack_vector: Any application deserializing untrusted data with pickle.loads()
remediation: Never unpickle data from untrusted sources. Use JSON, MessagePack, or Protocol Buffers instead.

nodes.label: Attacker Input
nodes.description: Malicious pickle bytes crafted by attacker
nodes.security_significance: Entry point — no validation occurs before deserialization begins
nodes.mitigation: Reject all pickle data from untrusted sources at the boundary

nodes.label: pickle.loads()
nodes.security_significance: Calls __reduce__ on any object type without restriction
nodes.mitigation: Replace with safe alternatives; use pickletools.dis for static analysis only

nodes.label: __reduce__ hook
nodes.security_significance: Allows attacker to specify any callable and arguments for execution
nodes.mitigation: Implement a custom Unpickler that restricts allowed globals

nodes.label: REDUCE opcode
nodes.description: Pickle REDUCE opcode (0x52) invokes the callable
nodes.security_significance: Core opcode that triggers arbitrary function call
nodes.mitigation: Scan for REDUCE opcode presence before deserialization

nodes.label: os.system()
nodes.security_significance: Achieves arbitrary OS command execution with the process's privileges
nodes.mitigation: Block the os module in custom Unpickler.find_class()

name: Python Pickle subprocess.Popen
description: Variant of the __reduce__ gadget chain targeting subprocess.Popen for more reliable command execution with argument control, bypassing shells that restrict os.system.
attack_vector: Any Python application deserializing untrusted pickle data
remediation: Use a restricted Unpickler. Block subprocess, os, and builtins in find_class().

nodes.label: Attacker Payload
nodes.security_significance: No boundary check; payload accepted as legitimate data
nodes.mitigation: Implement strict allowlist of deserializable types

nodes.label: pickle.loads()
nodes.security_significance: Executes __reduce__ without type validation
nodes.mitigation: Use RestrictedUnpickler pattern

nodes.label: GLOBAL opcode
nodes.security_significance: Loads any importable Python object by module+attribute path
nodes.mitigation: Override find_class() to raise exception for disallowed modules

nodes.label: subprocess.Popen
nodes.description: Spawns a subprocess with attacker-controlled arguments
nodes.security_significance: Direct process creation bypassing shell restrictions
nodes.mitigation: Block subprocess module in Unpickler

name: Java CommonsCollections 1
description: Classic gadget chain using InvokerTransformer chained through LazyMap and AnnotationInvocationHandler. Achieves arbitrary Java reflection-based method invocation leading to Runtime.exec().
attack_vector: Java deserialization endpoints accepting serialized Java objects (RMI, JMX, HTTP object parameters)
remediation: Upgrade to Commons Collections 3.2.2+. Use SerialKiller or similar deserialization filter. Implement JEP 290 filters.

nodes.label: Serialized Object
nodes.description: Java serialized object stream with 0xACED0005 magic
nodes.security_significance: Java accepts any serializable class during readObject()
nodes.mitigation: Implement ObjectInputFilter (JEP 290) before readObject()

nodes.label: ObjectInputStream.readObject()
nodes.security_significance: Invokes readObject() on the deserialized class, triggering gadget chain
nodes.mitigation: Replace with filtered ObjectInputStream

nodes.label: AnnotationInvocationHandler
nodes.description: readObject() calls entrySet() on its memberValues map
nodes.security_significance: Triggers LazyMap.get() during deserialization
nodes.mitigation: Filter AnnotationInvocationHandler from deserialization stream

nodes.label: LazyMap.get()
nodes.security_significance: Invokes the transformer chain without explicit call from application
nodes.mitigation: Upgrade Commons Collections; avoid LazyMap with untrusted data

nodes.label: ChainedTransformer
nodes.security_significance: Orchestrates reflection calls to build Runtime.exec() invocation
nodes.mitigation: Block Transformer classes in deserialization filter

nodes.label: InvokerTransformer
nodes.security_significance: Core gadget: calls Method.DEHYDRATE() with attacker-controlled method and args
nodes.mitigation: Patch to 3.2.2; InvokerTransformer throws SecurityException on untrusted input

nodes.label: Runtime.exec()
nodes.security_significance: Remote code execution with JVM process privileges
nodes.mitigation: No mitigation at this stage — prevent reaching this node

name: Java CommonsCollections 6
description: Java-version-independent gadget chain using HashSet + TiedMapEntry + LazyMap to trigger InvokerTransformer. Works on Java 8u76+ where CC1 was patched via AnnotationInvocationHandler fix.
attack_vector: All Java RMI/JMX/HTTP deserialization endpoints with Commons Collections on classpath
remediation: Upgrade Commons Collections. Implement JEP 290 deserialization filters. Use serialization allowlists.

nodes.label: Serialized Payload
nodes.security_significance: Entry point — passes JVM version check unlike CC1
nodes.mitigation: Block HashSet+TiedMapEntry combination in deserialization filter

nodes.label: HashSet.readObject()
nodes.security_significance: Standard JDK class that cannot be filtered without breaking functionality
nodes.mitigation: Use allowlist-based filtering instead of blocklist

nodes.label: TiedMapEntry.hashCode()
nodes.description: hashCode() calls getValue() which calls map.get(key)
nodes.security_significance: Bridges JDK collections to Commons Collections transformer chain
nodes.mitigation: Upgrade or filter TiedMapEntry

nodes.label: LazyMap.get()
nodes.security_significance: Same as CC1 LazyMap gadget, reachable via different path
nodes.mitigation: Upgrade Commons Collections

nodes.label: InvokerTransformer.transform()
nodes.security_significance: Executes Runtime.exec() via reflection
nodes.mitigation: Upgrade to fixed version where InvokerTransformer checks SecurityManager

nodes.label: Runtime.exec()
nodes.security_significance: Full RCE achieved
nodes.mitigation: Prevent reaching this node via input validation and deserialization filters

name: Java Spring Framework Gadget
description: Uses Spring's SerializableTypeWrapper and MethodInvokeTypeProvider to DEHYDRATE arbitrary methods via deserialization. Requires Spring on the classpath.
attack_vector: Spring-based Java applications with deserialization endpoints
remediation: Upgrade Spring Framework. Disable Java serialization endpoint if not required.

nodes.label: Serialized Input
nodes.security_significance: Spring-specific entry point
nodes.mitigation: Disable HTTP invoker; upgrade Spring

nodes.label: MethodInvokeTypeProvider
nodes.security_significance: Spring utility enables arbitrary method invocation
nodes.mitigation: Filter Spring serializable classes from stream

nodes.label: SerializableTypeWrapper
nodes.security_significance: Bypasses direct method reference checks
nodes.mitigation: Upgrade to patched Spring version

nodes.label: ReflectionUtils.invokeMethod()
nodes.security_significance: Arbitrary method execution with application context privileges
nodes.mitigation: No mitigation at this stage

name: .NET TypeConfuseDelegateGadget
description: Exploits type confusion in .NET delegate invocation to execute arbitrary methods. Chains MulticastDelegate, Comparison<T>, and SortedSet to trigger code execution during BinaryFormatter deserialization.
attack_vector: Any .NET application using BinaryFormatter, SoapFormatter, or NetDataContractSerializer
remediation: Replace BinaryFormatter with System.Text.Json or DataContractSerializer with known types. BinaryFormatter is disabled by default in .NET 5+.

nodes.label: BinaryFormatter Input
nodes.security_significance: BinaryFormatter deserializes any type without restriction
nodes.mitigation: Disable BinaryFormatter via AppContext switch

nodes.label: BinaryFormatter.Deserialize()
nodes.description: Deserializes the object graph, executing ISerializable.GetObjectData callbacks
nodes.security_significance: No type validation — all types with SerializableAttribute are accepted
nodes.mitigation: Replace with safe serializer

nodes.label: SortedSet<T>
nodes.description: SortedSet.OnDeserialization() calls Comparer to sort elements
nodes.security_significance: Standard JDK-equivalent class that triggers comparison callbacks
nodes.mitigation: Filter SortedSet from deserialization stream

nodes.label: TypeConfuseDelegate
nodes.description: Type confusion between Comparison<T> and Func<Process,string> delegates
nodes.security_significance: Bypasses .NET delegate safety by confusing types during invocation
nodes.mitigation: No runtime mitigation — prevent reaching this node

nodes.label: Process.Start()
nodes.security_significance: Full RCE with .NET application privileges
nodes.mitigation: Prevent reaching this node

name: .NET ObjectDataProvider Gadget
description: ObjectDataProvider is a WPF data binding class that can DEHYDRATE arbitrary methods. When deserialized via XamlReader or ExpandedWrapper, it calls MethodName on ObjectInstance, achieving RCE via Process.Start().
attack_vector: .NET applications deserializing XAML or using BinaryFormatter with WPF types on classpath
remediation: Block ObjectDataProvider in deserialization streams. Use DataContractSerializer with known-types list.

nodes.label: Serialized XAML / Binary
nodes.description: XAML or binary payload containing ObjectDataProvider
nodes.security_significance: XAML is a markup language that instantiates .NET objects
nodes.mitigation: Never deserialize untrusted XAML

nodes.label: XamlReader.Load()
nodes.security_significance: Instantiates any .NET type reachable from XAML namespace
nodes.mitigation: Validate and sanitize XAML input; disable XamlReader for untrusted input

nodes.label: ObjectDataProvider
nodes.description: WPF data binding class that calls MethodName on ObjectInstance during data refresh
nodes.security_significance: Legitimate WPF class repurposed as gadget — hard to block without breaking WPF
nodes.mitigation: Block ObjectDataProvider in deserialization filter

nodes.label: Process.Start()
nodes.security_significance: Full code execution
nodes.mitigation: Prevent reaching via input validation

name: ML PyTorch Malicious Model
description: PyTorch model files (.pt, .pth) are ZIP archives containing pickle files for model weights and architecture. torch.load() calls pickle.loads() internally, making any malicious pickle payload embedded in a model file execute on load.
attack_vector: ML engineers loading model checkpoints from untrusted sources (model hubs, third-party repositories)
remediation: Use torch.load(..., weights_only=True) in PyTorch 2.x. Verify model file hashes. Use safetensors format.

nodes.label: Malicious .pt File
nodes.description: PyTorch model file with embedded malicious pickle payload
nodes.security_significance: Looks like a legitimate model file; magic bytes are ZIP not pickle
nodes.mitigation: Verify file hash from trusted source before loading

nodes.label: torch.load()
nodes.description: Extracts ZIP and calls pickle.loads() on model data
nodes.security_significance: No sandbox; executes arbitrary pickle in the calling process context
nodes.mitigation: Use weights_only=True parameter (PyTorch 2.x)

nodes.label: pickle.loads()
nodes.security_significance: Executes __reduce__ without restriction
nodes.mitigation: Use RestrictedUnpickler if loading pickle from model files is unavoidable

nodes.label: __reduce__ Payload
nodes.security_significance: Arbitrary code execution during model load
nodes.mitigation: No mitigation at this stage

nodes.label: subprocess.Popen()
nodes.security_significance: Full RCE on the data scientist's machine
nodes.mitigation: Prevent reaching via weights_only=True and hash verification

name: ML scikit-learn Malicious Model
description: scikit-learn models are serialized with joblib (which uses pickle internally). A maliciously crafted .pkl or .joblib file can execute arbitrary code when loaded with joblib.load() or pickle.loads().
attack_vector: ML pipelines loading models from shared storage, CI/CD pipelines fetching models from registries
remediation: Use ONNX export for model interchange. Verify model checksums. Load models in isolated containers.

nodes.label: Malicious .pkl File
nodes.description: scikit-learn model file with embedded exploit payload
nodes.security_significance: Indistinguishable from legitimate model file without hash verification
nodes.mitigation: Maintain cryptographic hashes of all model artifacts

nodes.label: joblib.load()
nodes.description: Loads the model file; calls pickle.loads() internally
nodes.security_significance: No execution sandbox; runs in production process
nodes.mitigation: Load models in isolated subprocess or container

nodes.label: pickle.loads()
nodes.security_significance: Executes arbitrary __reduce__
nodes.mitigation: Validate bytes structure before passing to pickle

nodes.label: os.system() / subprocess
nodes.security_significance: RCE in production ML serving environment
nodes.mitigation: Prevent via input validation and model signing

name: Celery Task Deserialization
description: Celery task queues configured with pickle serialization accept task arguments as pickle payloads. An attacker with access to the message broker (Redis/RabbitMQ) can publish crafted task messages that execute arbitrary code on Celery workers.
attack_vector: Celery workers with CELERY_TASK_SERIALIZER='pickle' and accessible message broker
remediation: Set CELERY_TASK_SERIALIZER='json'. Restrict broker access. Use message authentication (CELERY_SECURITY_KEY).

nodes.label: Malicious Task Message
nodes.description: Pickle-serialized task message published to message broker
nodes.security_significance: Broker access may be insufficiently restricted in internal networks
nodes.mitigation: Enforce broker authentication and network segmentation

nodes.label: Message Broker (Redis/RabbitMQ)
nodes.description: Message broker routes task to worker queue
nodes.security_significance: Broker acts as amplifier — one message reaches all workers
nodes.mitigation: Enable broker authentication and TLS

nodes.label: Celery Worker
nodes.description: Worker receives message and deserializes task arguments
nodes.security_significance: Worker process has full application context and credentials
nodes.mitigation: Switch to JSON serializer

nodes.label: pickle.loads(args)
nodes.security_significance: Executes arbitrary code in worker process
nodes.mitigation: Set CELERY_TASK_SERIALIZER='json'; never use pickle for task args

nodes.label: RCE on Worker
nodes.description: Arbitrary command execution in worker environment
nodes.security_significance: Access to all secrets, databases, and internal services the worker has
nodes.mitigation: Prevent via serializer configuration and broker access control
